newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar trades tiny range to close unchanged.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar trades tiny range to close unchanged.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar traded a tiny range to close unchanged on Tuesday after the local market slapped it down sharply from overnight highs.

The currency reached US$0.6970 in offshore trading, within striking instance of an eight-year high of 0.6979, but came abruptly back down to earth to trade a tight 0.6948-51 range in the New Zealand session.
Dealers said there was a distinct lack of interest, and local traders were more bearish about the political situation than their counterparts offshore.
"I get the feeling that the local guys are still concerned with the political outlook and the offshore guys aren't and that's the difference," a Wellington dealer said.

"I think the offshore market looks to the (Eurokiwi) issues that are coming out and the yield at the moment," he added. The latest in a stream of Eurokiwis was a NZ$100 million issue by Hambros on behalf of the World Bank.
The dealer said he expected the offshore market to take the currency higher again overnight, with a likely range of 0.6945-60.
Locals are increasingly preoccupied with the October 12 general election, the first under proportional representation.
The governing National Party is currently polling between 35 and 40 percent but opposition Labour, New Zealand First and the Alliance are jointly drawing more than 50 percent support.
Bankers Trust said in a commentary earlier this week the Kiwi was at "artificially high" levels given the looming election, thanks to the ongoing Euro and Samurai interest.

It said the currency could be a casualty of a likely widening of the central bank's 0-2 percent inflation if there is a change of government, and was therefore likely to come under pressure as the election neared.
It said a drying up of Samurai issues and TWI-selling above 66.0 would also combine to cap the currency.
